argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than a clean certification claim. The admissible record supports certification only if the current release packet itself reflects the current evaluation results and plainly discloses the clinical-trial intake regression as a material limitation for that named launch use case. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release readiness in general, and public governance guidance supports deployment with measured, documented, and monitored risks, but prior family approval and the informal monitoring comment are contextual only and cannot substitute for current-release documentation or approved mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed for this position. The requested treatment is based on a narrower policy reading from the admissible record, not on launch-pressure considerations.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not require every weakness to be resolved before certification; it requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. On the present admissible record, the defensible policy reading is therefore caveated: aggregate pass plus no severity-one incidents can support certification only when paired with current disclosure of the subgroup weakness. The same admissible evidence does not support treating prior approval or informal monitoring alone as satisfying the policy.
concessions: The current record does not include the actual current release documentation or model-card text showing that the clinical-trial intake weakness was disclosed.
The current record does not include approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness before launch.
Prior approval of the same model family is stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry the certification decision.
The informal monitoring comment is not equivalent to reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
